# Project: Customer Churn Prediction (learning project for ML and AI role interviews)

## How to work with me
1. I am learning. Do ONE small task per prompt. If a prompt seems big, do only the smallest useful piece and tell me what is left.
2. Before writing code, tell me in 3-4 plain sentences what you will do and why.
3. Keep code short and simple. Small functions, clear names, comments that explain WHY, no clever tricks.
4. After writing code, explain it in plain language like I am a beginner. Define every technical term the first time you use it.
5. Always run the code and show me the real output. NEVER invent numbers, metrics, or results. Only report what actually ran. If you cannot run something, tell me the exact command to run myself.
6. Ask me before installing large packages or making a decision with trade-offs.
7. Commit to git after each step with a clear message (propose the command and I will approve it).

## The Word guide (most important rule)
The root file PROJECT_GUIDE.docx is my interview study material. After EVERY step:
1. Create or update a markdown file in docs/guide/ named NN_short_title.md (NN = step number).
2. Run `python tools/build_guide.py` to regenerate PROJECT_GUIDE.docx in the root. If you cannot run it, tell me to run it.
3. Tell me what you added to the guide.
4. Every guide chapter must be detailed enough to teach a beginner, not a summary: include at least 5 interview questions with full model answers; explain each step in "How it works" with a small concrete example; and quote the real code lines in the Code walkthrough and explain them.
5. Do only what the prompt asks. Do not add unrequested files, guide chapters, or git changes.

Every guide section must contain these headings, in plain easy language, in detail:
- What we built
- Why it matters (and which part of a real ML analyst or ML engineer job it matches)
- How it works, step by step
- Code walkthrough (explain the important lines)
- Data flow (what goes in, what happens, what comes out)
- Terms explained
- What could go wrong
- Interview questions with model answers
- Check yourself (2-3 questions)

Never shorten or delete earlier guide sections. Only edit them to fix mistakes.
Real results (metrics, counts) go in the guide only after they have been produced by running code.
